title: Starter Loop Playlist and Pair-Programming Recipes (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a compact, instructor-led starter loop that pairs a new engineer or integrator with a DX buddy to land a minimal Redwood SDK flow end-to-end in 45–90 minutes. Focus: confidence > completeness. Ship a runnable demo, capture telemetry, and leave with two repeatable artifacts: a minimal README and a short recorded terminal/screen snippet (for future micro-tutorials).

Intended audience:
- New hires in app/product teams evaluating Redwood for a feature
- Solutions/SEs running a fast POC with a customer
- Internal engineers running internal demos for PMs

High-level goals (success metrics):
- Time-to-first-successful-generation <= 30 minutes for most participants
- Telemetry shows successful API call + token usage event + latency metric in < 60m after session
- Participant can explain three levers to control cost/latency: batching, model variant, caching

Why pair-programming?
- Removes friction: one person navigates docs, the other implements and asks clarifying questions
- Encourages conversation about tradeoffs (latency vs cost) while code is live
- Easier to capture questions/obstacles for future docs improvements

Setup pre-reqs (to ask before session starts):
- Participant has a Redwood account and API key (or temporary demo key)
- Local machine: Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, git, curl
- Optional: Docker installed if we run local emulation (devkit).

Files to seed in a sandbox repo (starter template):
- README.md (one-paragraph gist + run steps)
- example/node/quickstart.js (minimal request + streaming example commented)
- example/python/quickstart.py
- prompts/initial_prompt.md (short system + user guidance)
- telemetry/README.md (how to read demo telemetry in console)

Playlist (45–90 minute flow) — prioritize as time allows:
1) 5m: Context + expected outcomes (show final demo)
2) 5–10m: Environment check + create API key together (if needed)
3) 10m: Minimal generation path
   - Implement the single-file example that performs a completion/chat call and prints response
   - Validate with a simple prompt: "Summarize this paragraph in 1 sentence"
4) 10–15m: Add streaming or function-calling example
   - Quick note on event parsing and UX
5) 10–15m: Observability + telemetry
   - Hook a minimal telemetry event (e.g., client.record_event or a snippet that logs tokens/latency)
   - Walk through Console -> Request trace -> Token cost breakdown (if tenant has Console access)
6) 10m: Cost/Performance knobs demo
   - Switch model variant (ft/quantized) and rerun
   - Show effect of batch size for a small synthetic load (explain how batching reduces per-token overhead)
7) 5–10m: Wrap-up + next steps (A/B test ideas, evaluate prompts)

Pair programming roles and recipes:
- Driver (writes code) / Navigator (reads docs, suggests next steps). Rotate at the 30-min mark if both are devs.
- If session is Solutions-led with a customer: SE is Navigator, customer dev is Driver.

Quick recipes (copy-paste snippets to include in starter templates):
- Minimal Node snippet (commented):
  const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference');
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
  async function run(){
    const r = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rwd-small-v1', messages: [{role:'user', content:'Explain mutexes like I am 10.'}] });
    console.log(r.output);
  }
  run();

- Streaming note: include an event handler example and explain backpressure briefly.

Telemetry checklist (must-haves to capture during session):
- event:demo_first_success (boolean)
- telemetry:api_latency_ms (median)
- telemetry:tokens_used
- tag:starter_template_version (git sha)
- store a small JSON to telemetry/manifest.json in the repo as an anchor for QA

Common friction points (observed in past sessions):
- Missing API key or wrong scopes — make key creation a live checklist item
- CORS surprises for web-based quickstarts — offer a simple Node proxy example
- Streaming parsers — suggest a helper util in the template that emits full messages every N tokens
- Confusion between hosted vs. dedicated endpoint URLs — add a short note near top of README

Templates and artifacts to produce by end of session:
- README snippet (3–5 steps): 1) set API key, 2) npm install, 3) node example, 4) open Console and confirm trace
- Short recording (~2–3 minutes) of the terminal run saved to /assets/demos/<owner>-<date>.mp4
- Issue opened in docs backlog with label "onramp-obs" and link to any questions encountered

Session facilitation tips for DX lead/SE:
- Keep language pragmatic: "we'll make one call that you can copy into your app; later we optimize"
- If stuck >8 minutes, pivot to a pre-built working branch and walk through differences
- Actively capture exact error messages into the session notes (we use these for search terms in docs)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include a default prompts/guardrails file for PII redaction? (privacy asks from compliance)
- Can we ship a tiny web-based widget that demonstrates streaming without CORS setup? (design/feasibility, ENG-5198)
- Add a tiny GitHub Action that runs the quickstart smoke test on PRs to the starter repo? (ops + infra cost eval)

Follow-ups (owners assigned):
- Marco: build node proxy example + PR (target: 2025-03-14)
- Jenny: prototype the telemetry manifest and small GH action (target: 2025-03-21)
- Aisha: synth a 2-min demo recording and upload to assets (target: 2025-03-07)

Notes-to-self / rapid backlog items:
- Create a 1-page "cheat sheet" that lists the three knobs (batching, model variant, caching) with one sentence each and expected unit effects (latency/cost)
- Add a troubleshooting section with 6 common error messages and one-line fixes

References and inspiration:
- internal: CON-quickstart-templates (Confluence)
- competitor research: short notes on different onboarding flows from other LLM API providers (kept offline)

End of draft — this is intentionally lightweight and prescriptive for running live sessions. Capture any edges from the first 10 run-throughs and we will iterate to a v1 in CONFLUENCE and copy a trimmed version into the public SDK repo docs.
